doc.title: Joseph Rene and Edna Kelly Interview, 1969-12-15

chapter: Joe Rene: Lewis, the Rena band and New Orleans
title: George Lewis learns by ear; neighbours of the first Dixieland band
summary: Lewis never learned to read music but became a fine jazz player. The talk turns to the first Dixieland band living around the corner.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: I tried to get him to learn how to read but it seemed like he could more at ease from here. Yes. And he turned out to be a real good, good class, good jazz class. Yes. And around the corner from there, there where Shield used to live. Remember the Dixieland band, the first Dixieland band? Yes.
Yes, I know. Tin Roof. Yeah.
Well, they were living right around the corner. Around from Governor Nichols?
Yeah, right there, yeah, on the street between Governor Nichols and Barracks. There in the shop there used to. And that boy just came up on the planet just like that. Yeah.
And he got the planes, so everybody warned him, you know. Who were you talking about now, George? George Lewis, yeah. A lot of fellas warned him.
